name: Burn-in, two hours
_note: Leave this running unattended. It drives the high-side outputs and the relays, watches the two board temperatures and the reference, and stops by itself. Nothing has to be wired: with no load connected it still exercises the drivers, the timing and the analog front end. ⚠️ Relays cycle every 30 s on purpose - the HF41F is rated 3x10^4 operations, and cycling once a second would spend a quarter of that in one run. See porttool_soak.c.

steps._note: 245 frames at 30 s is a little over the two hours the board itself is timing, so the last frames collected are the ones after it finished - that is how done=1 gets judged. The board stops driving at its own deadline whatever the PC does.

checks._note: vdda= is the ADC reference, not VDDA: VREFBUF drives VREF+ to a nominal 2.5 V and a healthy board reads about 2501 mV (measured 2026-09-08). The 2000-3600 band this replaces would have passed a board whose VREFBUF had failed and left VREF+ sitting near 3.3 V.

steps._note: The soak releases its own outputs when it finishes, and again on stop. This is the belt-and-braces one, for the case where the run was cut short.
